poster.title: The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida
poster.bookFirstPublication: 2020 (as Chats With the Dead); retitled form 2022
poster.bookOrigin: Sri Lankan English-language novel by Shehan Karunatilaka, set in Colombo. First published in India as Chats With the Dead in 2020; the retitled form appeared in 2022. Work context is distinct from the edition’s publishing location.
poster.creator: Cover artist uncredited in the linked record
poster.alt: White stacked title words cross a bright mask with curling upper forms, round eyes, a red nose and a toothed mouth; a Booker winner mark and Penguin emblem occupy the upper corners.
poster.blurb: A colourful face looks out through a tall stack of white words.

notes.title: Writing and image-making
notes.body: The publisher identifies the author and Indian imprint but does not name the cover artist. The displayed mask is discussed through visible shapes without assigning an unsupported ritual identity.

notes.title: A visible design relationship
notes.body: Rounded eyes and cheeks contrast with the narrow crest and long curved green fangs. The title remains white across these changing colours.

studyData.intro: White title words cross a bright mask with rounded eyes and long green fangs. The current Penguin India image carries a Booker winner mark, so its pictured printing is not assumed to share the catalogue’s September 2022 date.

regions.label: A title crosses the whole face
regions.summary: The title forms a tall stack of white words from the forehead to the chin.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: The title forms a tall stack of white words from the forehead to the chin. Its letters cross several different colours and facial features.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The same light lettering unites a very changeable painted field. Reading the title and recognising the face become intertwined rather than separate tasks.

sections.heading: The title keeps its wording across the image
sections.body: The English title is broken into a tall sequence of lines. The words remain one title even as they cross forehead, eyes, mouth and chin; the visible green fangs obscure parts of some lower letters.
sections.originalText: The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida
sections.translation: The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida

regions.question: Do you read the words or recognise the face first when the cover is small?

regions.label: One eye holds a turquoise centre
regions.summary: The eye on the viewer’s left has a turquoise inner area, a small darker pupil and a pale pink surround.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: The eye on the viewer’s left has a turquoise inner area, a small darker pupil and a pale pink surround. Rounded bands enclose it.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The strong circular geometry gives the face an immediate point of recognition. The unusual colour relationships keep it from becoming a naturalistic portrait.

regions.question: Which ring of colour makes this eye most noticeable?

regions.label: The other eye changes the colour order
regions.summary: The viewer’s right eye uses a pink inner disc inside turquoise and darker blue-green bands.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: The viewer’s right eye uses a pink inner disc inside turquoise and darker blue-green bands. Its small pupil sits off the centre.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The two eyes are related without being identical. Their colour reversal and unequal pupils can make the face feel animated rather than perfectly symmetrical.

regions.question: How does reversing the eye colours change the expression you perceive?

regions.label: A red bridge between eyes and mouth
regions.summary: A broad red nose occupies the centre below the eyes.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: A broad red nose occupies the centre below the eyes. Orange-red oval areas sit inside it and the white word of crosses the region above.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The warm nose interrupts the cooler eye colours and links the upper face to the mouth. Its broad horizontal shape also counters the long vertical title stack.

regions.question: What would change if the nose used the same turquoise as the eyes?

regions.label: Short teeth and long curved fangs
regions.summary: Short pale rounded or tapered teeth sit inside the dark mouth.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: Short pale rounded or tapered teeth sit inside the dark mouth. Longer green fangs curve down on either side and overlap parts of the lower title.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The small repeated teeth create a rhythm that differs from the sweeping fangs. That contrast makes the mouth expressive without requiring every tooth to be a sharp triangle.

regions.question: How do the short teeth and long fangs create different kinds of visual energy?

regions.label: A narrow point rises above the face
regions.summary: A tall red-orange pointed form rises between the curling upper shapes.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: A tall red-orange pointed form rises between the curling upper shapes. It narrows sharply towards the top of the cover.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The point stretches the face vertically while the eyes and side lobes widen it. These competing directions help the mask occupy the full tall format.

regions.question: How does this one narrow point affect the proportions of the whole face?

regions.label: Large upper loops enclose colour
regions.summary: Broad curled forms occupy both upper sides of the mask.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: Broad curled forms occupy both upper sides of the mask. Dark bands enclose bright pink, orange, red and green areas.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The loops establish a sweeping rhythm before the smaller eyes and mouth are read. Their unequal colours prevent the near-bilateral layout from feeling mechanically mirrored.

regions.question: Where do the two sides match in shape but differ in colour?

regions.label: Round side lobes widen the face
regions.summary: Large rounded lobes extend from both sides of the lower face.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: Large rounded lobes extend from both sides of the lower face. Small contrasting circles sit within their purple, blue and green fields.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: These broad forms balance the narrow crest above. Their simple round geometry also repeats the eyes at a much larger scale.

regions.question: How would the face’s balance change without these wide side forms?

regions.label: A winner mark in the corner
regions.summary: A white outlined device at the upper left reads The Booker Prize 2022 Winner.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: A white outlined device at the upper left reads The Booker Prize 2022 Winner. Its compact upright stack differs from the large central title.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The corner mark adds a publishing message without taking over the face. Its crisp white geometry also shares the title’s colour, keeping it within the cover’s visual system.

sections.heading: A catalogue date is not a printing date
sections.body: Penguin catalogues paperback ISBN 9780143459675 as September 2022, while the current image says Booker Prize 2022 Winner. The winning mark belongs to a later state than the pre-award catalogue date. The exact pictured printing and cover-design date are not established by that listing.

regions.question: How does a prize mark change what you expect from a book before reading its description?

regions.label: An author line below the mask
regions.summary: Shehan Karunatilaka appears in white capitals across the lower edge.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: Shehan Karunatilaka appears in white capitals across the lower edge. The line is smaller than the title and sits on a changing painted background.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The long line provides a final horizontal anchor after the face and title stack. Repeating white connects authorship to the title without giving both the same scale.

sections.heading: Sri Lankan work, Indian edition
sections.body: Penguin identifies Karunatilaka as a Sri Lankan writer and describes the novel’s setting as Colombo in 1990. The pictured product is an India Penguin edition. The story’s cultural setting and the edition’s publishing location are therefore kept distinct rather than reduced to one country label. Penguin’s announcement also records an earlier Indian publication in 2020 as Chats With the Dead, before the retitled 2022 form. This earlier publication is retained in the work metadata.

regions.question: What makes this smaller author line feel like the cover’s closing statement?

regions.label: Colour remains outside the face
regions.summary: Turquoise, pink and other painted colour remains around the mask’s outer contours.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: Turquoise, pink and other painted colour remains around the mask’s outer contours. Uneven textures are visible within the apparently flat bright areas.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The ground continues the cover’s energy outside the face rather than isolating it on neutral paper. The changes of hue help the dark outer contours stay visible.

regions.question: Where is the face easiest to separate from the colourful field around it?
